Good range hood, poor light - A very well made range hood. It looks good and was easy to install. The fan is pretty loud at the highest setting, but I found that the lower settings are powerful enough that (at least, so far), I have not needed the "full" power. The light, however, is a different matter. Compared to our previous range hood, which had two halogen bulbs, the light from the 2 LED bulbs is pitiful. It barely provides enough light for the front two burners, and is completely insufficient for the rear burners. In addition, the light has color distortion towards the edges, which makes it hard to gauge doneness/color of the food being cooked. If the hood had better lights, it would have easily rated a 5.

Some thoughts on installation: This hood is not exactly light (which I consider a good thing, except during installation). I would recommend having a second person available for installation - I can not see how one person would be able to do this by themselves. In addition, I would recommend laying the hood flat on the stove, and measuring up to the cabinet where it is to be mounted. Then cut two boards to that length (or just a little bit short of that, for some wiggle room). This will allow you to prop up the hood, in the correct position, underneath the cabinet, which is very helpful for marking the holes to drill and installing the screws. I also found that the screws that were provided were far too long for the our cabinets - they would have stuck out on the inside the cabinet. I found screws with similar heads that were about 3/4" shorter, and those worked just fine.

Convenient Means to Making Ice - We have issues with our ice maker in our refrigerator. It is far too slow to produce ice and we have considered getting another refrigerator because of it. We usually just buy bags of ice to solve the problem, but for convenience sake, I decided to get this Frigidaire ice maker.

Compact in size, this ice maker sits on the countertop and produces just enough ice to make it useful for beverages and other modest needs. You just open the flip top, pour in water, and wait about 10 to 15 minutes for the first batch of cubes of ice to be made. The small cubes are bell/gumdrop shaped and are small enough to fit in tight spaces, making them good for those who want to add ice to, say, water bottles and other receptacles that cannot handle normal sized ice cubes.

The outside of this ice maker has lights that indicate Ice Full, Add Water, and Ice Making. The top two indicators display a red light, to get your attention The one annoyance I have with this ice maker is that the ice tends to stack up in the back, which triggers the sensor and causes the ‘Ice Full’ light to come on. There could, in fact, be plenty of space in the ice bin and you will need to open, pull the ice down from the back, and close to make the ice maker resume. The problem is that the ice is dumped in back and stacks up on the back edge. A change to the engineering- having it dump the ice in the middle of the ice container, for example- would fix this problem.

Other than that, this Frigidaire ice maker works well and produces the necessary ice to use in beverages for my family of four. It takes up little space and you can easily flip open the lid to get the ice you need. It’s a good investment for those who have a faulty ice maker in the fridge and who are tired of making regular trips to the store to purchase bags of ice.
